name: loka-wikidata-v12
notes: Second model in the normalized-wikidata series. Trained on the v12-100k corpus (671,817 clean triples, ~1.9x the size of v11's v11-50k corpus) using the same 44.5M-parameter BPE architecture. Per-epoch trajectory was disrupted by another LLaMA 3.1 8B experiment sharing the laptop's 8 GB GPU mid-training: epochs 2-4 ran cleanly at 32-41 min each (ppl 343.18 -> 238.05 -> 226.86, hitting the v12 best at epoch 4), then epochs 5-7 went to 175-191 min each as GPU contention corrupted Adam's momentum state and the loss diverged (ppl 243.59 -> 250.82 -> 257.77). Training process was killed externally at epoch 7. We ship the epoch-6 snapshot (taken before the divergence got worse) at ppl 250.82. Even degraded, v12 is meaningfully better than v11 (ppl 279.12 at 3 epochs) — the bigger and cleaner corpus is showing through. A clean retrain on an exclusive GPU would land closer to the epoch-4 trajectory (~225 ppl). Pinning the epoch-6 ckpt for the series consistency; future cycles may revisit v12 with a clean retrain. Companion dataset on HF: EmmaLeonhart/normalized-wikidata tag v12-100k.
